question: What additional line-drawing and kuśa-covering acts are performed on the fire-pit?
premises: The center is taken using two darbha blades.
The walls are covered with kuśa.
Upward lines are drawn on the three east-facing lines and kuśa is placed outside.
inference: The fire-pit is further defined and protected through central marking, line-drawing, and kuśa coverings inside and outside.
uncertainties: The precise geometry of the east-facing and upward lines is not fully clear from the verse alone.
plain_english: The center is taken with two darbha blades, the walls are covered with kuśa, upward lines are drawn on the three east-facing lines, and kuśa is also placed outside.
